h: Teshuvah and Trust Turn Affliction Into Shabbos Delight

it is turned for him into a nega of tzaraas."

of the people of the world who are called

p: these are for the slaves and maidservants,
to eat, to drink and to rejoice.'
the parshah of nega'im, they became afraid.
Moshe said to them: 'Do not be afraid;
to eat, to drink and to rejoice.'"
Now this needs to be understood:
after all, the parshah of nega'im
do not become impure through nega'im
(as stated at the beginning of chapter 3 of Nega'im).
"Many are the pains of the wicked" (Tehillim 32:10),
But regarding this one may say
אַךְ אַחַר כָּךְ הֵבִיא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
But afterward it brings in Midrash Rabbah
"Many are the pains of the wicked."
"And He said: If you will diligently listen, etc.,
I will not place upon you."
And this needs to be understood:
of "if you will diligently listen, etc.,"
that "I will not place all the sickness
"Since He does not place it, why a cure?"
along the lines of what they said in the Midrash
That is, that there should be the desire
to hear the words of Torah.
And this is "If you will diligently listen, etc.,
and give ear to His mitzvos":
שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים יִהְיֶה לָכֶם חֵשֶׁק
that at least you have the desire
even if you spoil things in actual deed,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הִבְטִיחַ לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
nevertheless HaKadosh Baruch Hu promised them:
"All the sickness that I placed upon Egypt
I will not place upon you."
the plagues were for them only as punishment,
"One more plague (nega) I will bring, etc.";
for the blow was at the root,
that with each plague Yisrael went out
of the ten traits of holiness,
the blow was at their root,
And this is "I will not place upon you,
for I am Hashem your Healer":
the blow must come like nega'im,
it will be only by way of healing,
that it be an altar of atonement,
And this is why it says "I will not place upon you":
"but he who loves him disciplines him early" (Mishlei 13:24),
as they said in Midrash Rabbah
even though it was crushing labor
For whatever is not sufferings of love,
אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְכִּיר שְׁמוֹ
HaKadosh Baruch Hu does not mention His Name
as they said in the Midrash
but rather 'and the darkness He called night'"
(וְעַיֵּין תּוֹסָפוֹת תַּעֲנִית ג, א דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְאִלּוּ)
And in the parshah of rebuke
they are all written with the Name Havayah,
which is the Name of mercy;
"he who loves him disciplines him early."
which are not sufferings of love
then only at a time of
when Hashem Yisbarach sends the cure
And this is what they said (Sanhedrin 107a):
"Is that man to be driven out so much?
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him:
Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav:
For six months David was afflicted with tzaraas, etc."
וְאִם הָיָה מַגִּיעַ לוֹ עוֹנֶשׁ זֶה
Now if this punishment was due to him,
לָמָּה לֹא שָׁלַח לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
why did Hashem Yisbarach not send it to him?
And King David, alav hashalom, asked:
But about him there was written
the sin of a blemish of the bris,
which is reckoned in Midrash Rabbah
עַל עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נְגָעִים בָּאִים כוּ׳
"Nega'im come because of ten things, etc.,
and because of forbidden relations, etc.";
and so it is in the Gemara (Arachin 16a).
And regarding nega'im they said in the Gemara
that they are not sufferings of love;
and there are two answers in the Gemara:
"This is for us, and that is for them,"
"This is in private, that is in public."
And as is written in the holy Zohar
He strikes him openly upon his face, etc."
for these are not of love.
And the two answers are one:
even though the nega'im are in a hidden place,
since he is sent out of the camp,
And with King David, alav hashalom,
who required the punishment of nega'im,
and the Sanhedrin separated from him,
as they said in the Gemara there,
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him,
does not attach His Name to evil,
as it says, "I will not place upon you";
that it be for him an altar of atonement,
then: "for I am Hashem your Healer."
And this is what it says in the Midrash:
the parshah of nega'im, they became afraid":
since there can be such an impurity
that they will have to go outside
even from the camp of Yisrael,
who knows whether one will be included in
Moshe said to them: "Do not be afraid;
these are for the nations of the world,"
to whom HaKadosh Baruch Hu sends
sufferings that are not of love,
if you should need, Heaven forbid,
they too will be only for healing,
since the punishment of one who neglects the delight of Shabbos
is that it turns into a nega,
the reward for one who is healed of his nega
is to eat, to drink and to rejoice,
for it turns from nega into oneg.
"Many are the pains of the wicked,
but he who trusts in Hashem, kindness will surround him."
And this needs to be understood:
is the opposite of the wicked
"but the righteous, kindness will surround him."
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
But it is based on what is said
"The face of Hashem is against evildoers, etc."
"Evil" means one who blemishes the bris
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א ריט, ב
(as is written in the holy Zohar I 219b,
that is, crying out is effective for this.
for the one who blemishes is called wicked,
הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנֵא לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק
that is, one who hates the trait of tzaddik,
"Hashem redeems the soul of His servants,
and none who take refuge in Him will be condemned" (Tehillim 34:23).
for the righteous do not need redemption;
only "His servants" are those called so
who want to be His servants
and have a desire to be good,
and they are included among the servants of Hashem.
And since it says "will not be condemned,"
of one who deserves to be condemned;
but since he is among those who take refuge in Hashem,
who truly want to be good,
and when sufferings come upon them,
they are only an altar of atonement
And this is what it says in the Midrash:
"Many are the pains of the wicked"
that is, for one who is among those who hate the tzaddik,
who is among those who take refuge in Him,
even though the yetzer overpowers them,
nevertheless when sufferings come upon him
which are not among the sufferings of love,
nevertheless it is only for healing,
as it says, "I will not place upon you,"
and it is an altar of atonement.
And by being aroused to teshuvah,
he then merits that it be turned into oneg;
and this is "kindness will surround him":
it will surround him like an encompassing light,
even though the kindnesses will not be revealed;
nevertheless the end result will be for kindness,
about Rebbi, who was injured in his little finger,
and he judged that it was not sufferings of love,
"Many are the pains of the wicked."
"Had we not read on the matter (Eichah 4:20)
'The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Hashem,'
That is, he was caught in their sin,
as it says, "was caught in their corruptions";
and as is written in the holy Zohar
that he was punished because it was in his power to protest;
and for this sufferings came in public,
and he blemished in this, that he did not say good,
And this is why it brings from this pasuk
in order to merit to eat, to drink and to rejoice,
for this is the meaning of "kindness will surround him."
